name: Lahauli Tea (Salt Tea)
ingredients: Brick tea leaves or high-quality black tea leaves
Fresh yak milk or full-fat cow milk
Optional: A dollop of fresh butter (ghee or yak butter)
instructions: 1. Boil water in a large pot and add the tea leaves, letting them simmer until the water turns dark and concentrated.
2. Add a pinch of baking soda, which helps in extracting deep color and flavor from the tea leaves.
3. Add salt to taste and simmer for a few more minutes.
4. Pour in the milk and stir continuously, allowing the mixture to froth and turn a creamy light brown color.
5. Optionally, whisk in a small piece of butter or ghee for added richness.
6. Serve hot, traditionally in bowls or tea cups, often accompanied by roasted barley flour (sattu).
description: Lahauli Tea, also known as Butter Tea or Gur-Gur Chai in parts of the Himalayas, is a vital beverage in the high-altitude cold deserts of Lahaul and Spiti. It is not just a drink but a survival essential, providing necessary hydration, warmth, and high-calorie energy to the locals living in harsh, freezing conditions.
